$comment: States a format that is already in use; changes nothing in it. Source: adcut's adcut/contracts.py (contract A) and the video-ads skill pack's docs/contract.md. A TSV contract: the schema describes one row, each cell is text (README, 'Two formats').
title: ads.creatives/1
description: A creatives manifest: one row per exported creative file. A maker writes it beside its upload sheet; an operator reads it to find a report row's creative by the code in the material's name.
x-rules: The first line is '# ads.creatives/1'; the old mark '# cads.creatives/1' is refused by adcut's reader and still read by the video-ads skill pack's.
No cell of the six columns is blank, and no cell holds a tab or a line break.
A code is on one row only.
A code's md5 never changes: the reader refuses a later manifest that moves it.
A material id is on one row only, per platform.
A later version only adds columns at the end.

code.description: The creative's code with its check digit (for example DEMO-0007-6): the token the material's name carries, so the reader finds codes in names by these strings alone and knows nothing of their format.

md5.description: The exported file's MD5, 32 lowercase hex digits.

platform.description: The reader's platform id for where the file goes (for example qianchuan for douyin).

exported_at.description: When the file was exported: ISO 8601 with its zone.

product.description: The product the creative is for.

material_ids.description: Optional, last. The ids the platform gave the file once it was uploaded (千川's 素材ID): digits, separated by ';'. Written only when a row has one; blank on a row without. The reader maps report rows filed under these ids to the code.
